source_locator: R2298: B.I.20/a, Skierski, 3 September, command post at folwark Włosty, battle south of Grudusk
current_activity: division headquarters at folwark Włosty during the fighting south of Grudusk
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-03, cited below. Skierski (PISM B.I.20/a, R2298) says that after the night march of 2-3 September 1939 the division arrived in the area south of Grudusk, organized a defence, and that the division commander’s command post was at folwark Włosty. The division then attacked toward Grudusk and, under a later army order, toward Przasnysz; by the end of the day the situation had come apart. A later itinerary in the same file places folwark Włosty, and a second echelon at Regimin, north of Ciechanów on 3 September. The pin is the manor at Włosty at 5 km. The existing 1 September Mława claim is left unchanged. Event definition: A dated headquarters, movement, engagement, defensive assignment or surrender location in the September 1939 campaign. Event support: PISM B.I.20/a (R2298), the typed after-action account of Kpt. dypl. Stanisław Skierski, quartermaster of the 8th Infantry Division. Memory account, uneven; he says his papers were destroyed at the Modlin capitulation and that some dates are only approximate. Used at confidence 0.5. Location and precision are given on the claim row. Review (Poland 1939, branch poland-1939, 28 November 2026): new row; old value none, new value this claim (confidence 0.5).

source_locator: R2298: B.I.20/a, Skierski, 12 September, battle of Zaborówek and Zaborów
current_activity: the division takes Zaborówek and Zaborów in the Kampinos fighting of 12 September
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-12, cited below. Skierski (PISM B.I.20/a, R2298) describes the battle of Zaborówek after the division had left Modlin on 11 or 12 September 1939 for the southern edge of the Kampinos Forest, on the Leszno–Babice track. On the morning of 12 September it was to attack toward Zaborów and Babice in concert with Gen. Thommée’s group; when that group did not attack, the 8th Division attacked alone, took Zaborówek without difficulty, took Zaborów after resistance, and late in the evening pursued toward Babice. The pin is Zaborówek at 5 km, covering neighbouring Zaborów. The existing 1 September Mława claim is not rewritten. source_locator: R2298: B.I.20/a, Skierski, 14 September, return to Modlin and start of the fortress defence
current_activity: the division is turned back to Modlin and assigned to defend the fortress from the east and south
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-14, cited below. Skierski (PISM B.I.20/a, R2298) says that on the night of 13-14 September 1939 Gen. Małachowski met the division on its march axis with an order to return at once to Modlin, because German forces had crossed the Narew between Zegrze and Nowy Dwór, and that during 14 September the division was turned north along the edge of the Kampinos Forest. A section headed as the defence of Modlin from 14 to 28 September says Operational Group Modlin was then formed under Gen. Thommée, and that the 8th Division was given the task of covering Modlin from the east and south. The pin is Modlin on 14 September, the day of the return and the start of that defence. source_locator: R2298: B.I.20/a, Skierski, 29 September, last day in the Modlin fortress
current_activity: the division spends its last day in the Modlin fortress after the capitulation
notes: Event date: sources covering 1939-09-29, cited below. Skierski (PISM B.I.20/a, R2298) says that the capitulation order was brought from Warsaw on the evening of 27 September or the morning of 28 September, that negotiations went on through 28 September while fighting continued, and that he himself learned of the capitulation later. He places the formalities in the fortress and says they remained there through 29 September, leaving on the night of 29-30 September with the last officer transport. The claim is dated 29 September, the last day he places the division in the fortress. Destroyed is left false; the event is a surrender.
